## Closing: Obsoleted by upstream Effect/Stream migration

This PR is no longer needed. The upstream codebase has undergone a major architectural migration to Effect/Stream/Runner that addresses all the race conditions this PR targeted. Our PR branches forked from `0bbf26a1ce` (Mar 20) and were pushed Mar 30 — the same day the final migration commit landed, making them effectively obsolete before they were even reviewed.

### Upstream commits that supersede this PR

| Commit | Date | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| [`860531c275`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/860531c275) | Mar 28 | `refactor(session): effectify session processor (#19485)` — Replaces raw `for await` iteration with `Effect/Stream` (`Stream.tap` → `Stream.runDrain`), making stream interruption native via `Fiber.interrupt`. The `cleanup()` function handles all dangling state (currentText, reasoningMap, pending tool parts). |
| [`c5442d418d`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/c5442d418d) | Mar 30 | `refactor(session): effectify SessionPrompt service (#19483)` — Introduces the `Runner` state machine with `SynchronizedRef`-based atomic state transitions. `Runner.cancel` → `Fiber.interrupt` propagates cleanly through the stream processing chain. |

### What this PR did vs what upstream now handles

| Our fix | Upstream solution |
|---------|-------------------|
| `Promise.race([iter.next(), aborted])` to prevent `for await` hang | `Effect/Stream` with `Stream.runDrain` — interruption is native via `Fiber.interrupt` |
| `abortChildren()` to kill child tool fibers | `cleanup()` in processor.ts marks all pending tools as error on abort |
| `sweep()` for dangling state | `cleanup()` handles `currentText`, `reasoningMap`, and pending tool parts |

Related: #20095, #20094
Superseded by: #19485, #19483

## Closing: Obsoleted by upstream Effect/Runner migration

This PR is no longer needed. The upstream codebase has undergone a major architectural migration to Effect/Stream/Runner that addresses all the race conditions this PR targeted, plus the `prompt_async` fire-and-forget issue was independently fixed. Our PR branches forked from `0bbf26a1ce` (Mar 20) and were pushed Mar 30 — the same day the final migration commit landed.

### Upstream commits that supersede this PR

| Commit | Date | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| [`814a515a8a`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/814a515a8a) | Mar 24 | `fix: improve plugin system robustness (#18280)` — Adds `.catch()` + `Bus.publish(Session.Event.Error)` to the `prompt_async` route, fixing the fire-and-forget unhandled rejection. Includes a test. |
| [`860531c275`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/860531c275) | Mar 28 | `refactor(session): effectify session processor (#19485)` — Effect/Stream replaces raw async iteration; interruption is native. |
| [`c5442d418d`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/c5442d418d) | Mar 30 | `refactor(session): effectify SessionPrompt service (#19483)` — Introduces the `Runner` state machine (`Idle → Running → Shell → ShellThenRun`) with `SynchronizedRef`-based atomic transitions. `Runner.Cancelled` replaces our `SessionCancelledError`. `ensureRunning` coalesces concurrent callers via `Deferred`. Fiber-based interruption propagates through `Deferred.await` in Permission/Question services, replacing our explicit `rejectSession()`. |

### What this PR did vs what upstream now handles

| Our fix | Upstream solution |
|---------|-------------------|
| Generation-guarded cancel (prevent stale cancel hitting new generation) | `Runner` state machine with fiber IDs — cancel only interrupts the current fiber |
| `precancelled` map (cancel before start) | `Runner.ensureRunning` + `SynchronizedRef` — atomic state transitions prevent lost cancels |
| `SessionCancelledError` | `Runner.Cancelled` error class |
| `rejectSession()` for Permission/Question on cancel | Effect interruption propagates through `Deferred.await` — pending Permission/Question awaits are interrupted when the fiber is interrupted |
| `prompt_async` fire-and-forget fix (planned addition) | Already fixed in `814a515a8a` with `.catch()` + `Bus.publish(Error)` |

Related: #20095, #20094, #14565, #19855
Superseded by: #19483, #19485, #18280

## Closing: Resolved by upstream Effect/Runner migration

All three failure modes described in this issue — plus the two additional trigger paths reported by @zswll2 — are now addressed by upstream's migration to Effect/Stream/Runner.

### Upstream commits that resolve this issue

| Commit | Date | What it fixes |
|--------|------|---------------|
| [`814a515a8a`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/814a515a8a) | Mar 24 | **`prompt_async` fire-and-forget** — Adds `.catch()` + `Bus.publish(Session.Event.Error)` to the `prompt_async` route. Includes a test. Fixes @zswll2's "followup queue auto-fire" trigger path. |
| [`860531c275`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/860531c275) | Mar 28 | **Abort-safe stream iteration** — Replaces raw `for await` with `Effect/Stream` (`Stream.runDrain`). Stream interruption is now native via `Fiber.interrupt`. `cleanup()` handles all dangling state. |
| [`c5442d418d`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/c5442d418d) | Mar 30 | **Cancel correctness** — Introduces the `Runner` state machine with `SynchronizedRef`-based atomic transitions. `Runner.cancel` → `Fiber.interrupt` eliminates stale-cancel and lost-cancel races. `ensureRunning` coalesces concurrent callers via `Deferred`. Effect interruption propagates through Permission/Question `Deferred.await`. |

### Original failure modes → resolution

1. **Lost cancel before start** → `Runner.ensureRunning` + `SynchronizedRef` atomic state transitions prevent this.
2. **Stale cancel aborting new generation** → `Runner` uses fiber IDs; cancel only interrupts the current fiber.
3. **Dangling permission/question waits after cancel** → Effect's interruption model propagates through `Deferred.await` in Permission/Question services. `addFinalizer` rejects all pending on scope close.

### @zswll2's additional trigger paths → resolution

4. **Followup queue auto-fire (`prompt_async`)** → `Runner.ensureRunning` coalesces concurrent callers (if running, joins via `Deferred` instead of racing). `prompt_async` `.catch()` handler (`814a515a8a`) catches errors and publishes them to the bus.
5. **ESC-on-Question race** → `Question.reject()` fails the specific `Deferred` with `RejectedError`; `Runner.cancel` interrupts the fiber. Either winning the race produces a clean outcome — processor sets `ctx.blocked` on `RejectedError`, or fiber interruption triggers cleanup. No hang, no unhandled error.

Closing PRs #20101 and #20102 as well — they targeted the old async/await architecture and are fully superseded.

## Closing: Resolved by upstream Effect/Stream migration

The stream iteration hang on abort described in this issue is resolved by the upstream migration from raw `for await` to Effect/Stream.

### Upstream commit

[`860531c275`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/860531c275) — `refactor(session): effectify session processor (#19485)` (Mar 28)

This commit replaces the raw `for await` loop over the LLM stream with `Effect/Stream` (`Stream.tap` → `Stream.runDrain`). Stream interruption is now native via `Fiber.interrupt` — when `Runner.cancel` interrupts the processing fiber, the stream drain is interrupted immediately without waiting for `iter.next()` to resolve. The `cleanup()` function handles all dangling state (currentText, reasoningMap, pending tool parts), preventing zombie sessions.

The `Runner` module introduced in [`c5442d418d`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/c5442d418d) — `refactor(session): effectify SessionPrompt service (#19483)` (Mar 30) — further solidifies this by providing a clean `cancel` → `Fiber.interrupt` pipeline.

See also: #20095 (parent issue, also closed)

This should be resolved by the upstream Effect/Runner migration.

[`c5442d418d`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/c5442d418d) — `refactor(session): effectify SessionPrompt service (#19483)` (Mar 30) introduces a `Runner` state machine that replaces the old `SessionPrompt.loop()` queueing. The `Runner` uses `SynchronizedRef`-based atomic state transitions with four states: `Idle`, `Running`, `Shell`, `ShellThenRun`.

Key changes relevant to this issue:
- **Concurrent `loop()` callers coalesce** — `Runner.ensureRunning` returns the same `Deferred` to all callers when a run is already in progress. No more queueing or hanging.
- **Cancel interrupts the fiber** — `Runner.cancel` does `Fiber.interrupt`, which propagates through `Deferred.await` in Permission/Question services. Pending waits are interrupted, not left dangling.
- **`Runner.Cancelled` error** — interrupted callers get a typed `Cancelled` error instead of hanging indefinitely.
- **Scope finalization** — `addFinalizer` on Permission/Question state rejects all pending deferreds on scope close.

We had a PR (#20102) targeting this with a different approach (generation-guarded cancel, `precancelled` map, explicit `rejectSession()`), but it was obsoleted by this architectural change before it could be merged. Closed it with details in the PR comment.

This should be resolved by two upstream changes:

1. [`814a515a8a`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/814a515a8a) — `fix: improve plugin system robustness (#18280)` (Mar 24) adds a `.catch()` handler to the `prompt_async` route that catches rejected promises and publishes them to the bus via `Bus.publish(Session.Event.Error, ...)` instead of letting them become unhandled rejections that bleed into stderr. This commit includes a test verifying the handler exists.

2. [`c5442d418d`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/c5442d418d) — `refactor(session): effectify SessionPrompt service (#19483)` (Mar 30) introduces a `Runner` state machine where cancel is handled via `Fiber.interrupt` with typed `Runner.Cancelled` errors. This eliminates the class of unhandled rejections that occurred when cancel raced with prompt processing — the interruption propagates cleanly through Effect's fiber model instead of producing uncaught promise rejections.

This is related to the recent update [v1.2.22](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v1.2.22) from Mar 8, 2026. I came back from vacation and noticed that all my sessiosn were gone. Upon looking in the `~/.local/share/opencode` folder, I noticed a large database file `opencode.db` (~900MB) and a "small one" (~600kB). Seems like the migration didn't happen on my end, so I had to delete the new files and rename my old ones to match the new schema.
In the end, this fixed my problem:
```sh
mv opencode-stable.db opencode-stable.db.backup
rm -f opencode-stable.db-shm opencode-stable.db-wal

cp opencode.db opencode-stable.db
cp opencode.db-wal opencode-stable.db-wal
cp opencode.db-shm opencode-stable.db-shm
```
I didn't mind losing my new data, since it was just one session.

Main problem with [ctrl]+[c]:
In the konsole or terminal, this means "end task".
OpenCode runs in a terminal session. To press only [ctrl]+[c] means, to end it.
Because of this, to copy something in the konsole or terminal, an additional [shift] keypress is required.

> Auto-subscribe to everything, not just config-specified URIs. In my project, the server exposes an inbox resource and we want to know the moment it changes. Requiring users to manually list every URI in config felt like unnecessary friction — if a server supports subscriptions, you probably want them. Config subscriptions still works for adding URIs that aren't in listResources().

One of the use cases I see for this feature, is exposing access to running production system, where each resource is a queue/listener.

This way agents could selectively subscribe to certain queues, depending on the task they're solving, and adopt their behavior accordingly. There might be hundreds of different resources, possibly more dynamically added.

In this light, auto-subscribing to all resources might be a bad idea.
